paper: Kavvas et al. 2018, Nat Commun 9:4306 — M. tuberculosis pan-genome ML AMR prediction
grounding: Questions are anchored to (a) what REPORT.md tested (MI + ensemble L1-SVM on 1,595-strain allele pan-genome, 13 drugs) and (b) what the paper claims but our replication did not resolve (C3 epistasis, C4 3-D structural mapping, lineage stratification, novel-marker generalization).

open_questions.q: Does the ensemble L1-SVM's advantage over pairwise MI hold when the classifier family is varied (Random Forest, gradient-boosted trees, deep MLP on allele one-hots) on the same 1,595-strain matrix, or is the ubiA/inhA/rpoC/gid recovery pattern an artifact of L1 sparsity + SGD hinge loss specifically?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §4.3 reproduces the L1-SVM ensemble but only that classifier family. The paper's headline is 'ML corroborates 33 known + 24 new signatures' — plural ML — yet only linear L1-SVM is exercised. If RF/GBM/DL recover a different additive set (or fail to recover ubiA), the '24 new' claim is classifier-conditional, not a genuine biological discovery.
open_questions.next_steps: Run RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=500, class_weight=balanced), XGBoost, and a shallow MLP on the same allele matrix with matched preprocessing (drop PE/PPE/PGRS + other-drugs' primary genes). Compare per-drug top-40 gene rankings vs the L1-SVM ensemble. Publish the concordance matrix. Free/uicgpu compute; hours, not days.

open_questions.q: Are the '24 new' AMR signatures the paper reports genuinely novel biological markers, or lineage/phylogenetic hitchhikers of the curated katG/rpoB/pncA/embB/gyrA/rpsL set that survive the paper's remove-primary-gene preprocessing but not a full phylogeny-aware confound test?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §5 and §7 explicitly flag that the RAxML core-SNP phylogeny was not rebuilt and that no lineage-corrected sensitivity analysis was run. The paper's own preprocessing removes each drug's primary gene from other drugs' analyses but does not phylogeny-correct the SVM. Novel-marker claims that ride on Lineage 2 Beijing MDR co-transmission would collapse under a matched-lineage subsample.
open_questions.next_steps: Build the RAxML core-SNP tree from cluster_info.csv core genes (paper: 2,803 core, 21,206 SNPs). Assign each strain to Lineage 1-7 via SNP barcode (Coll 2014). Rerun the ensemble L1-SVM on (a) a lineage-balanced subsample and (b) with a treeWAS / homoplasy-corrected association layer. Any 'novel' signature that survives both is genuinely novel; the rest are re-labelled as lineage-linked.

open_questions.q: How does per-drug SVM performance vary between drugs with distinct resistance-mechanism classes — isoniazid (katG/inhA prodrug activation), rifampicin (rpoB target-site mutation), pyrazinamide (pncA loss-of-function), fluoroquinolones (gyrA/gyrB target-site) — and does the L1-SVM systematically underperform on loss-of-function mechanisms where the resistant allele is a stop-codon/frameshift heterogeneous set rather than a small set of gain-of-function substitutions?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §4.3 shows pncA dropping to SVM rank 55 on pyrazinamide (137 R / 92 S) despite MI recovering pncA at rank 1. This is treated as a sample-size story, but pyrazinamide resistance is dominated by pncA loss-of-function (any-inactivating-mutation) whereas rifampicin resistance is dominated by rpoB RRDR gain-of-function. If loss-of-function drugs are systematically SVM-invisible, the paper's ML platform is drug-mechanism biased in a way not currently disclosed.
open_questions.next_steps: Stratify per-drug ROC-AUC / F1 by resistance mechanism class (target-site GoF vs LoF vs efflux vs prodrug activation). Report per-mechanism SVM sensitivity. Test whether replacing binary allele presence with per-gene 'any nonsynonymous variant' features closes the gap for pncA and ethA. Requires the allele->variant-annotation crosswalk (SnpEff on the aligned core genome), which the paper's data package does not directly provide.

open_questions.q: Do the paper's ML-recovered signatures generalize across the major M. tuberculosis lineages — Lineage 2 (Beijing, MDR-enriched) vs Lineage 3 (EAI) vs Lineage 4 (LAM/Haarlem/T) — under a leave-one-lineage-out cross-validation, or is per-drug performance dominated by the Beijing MDR strains that are overrepresented in PATRIC?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §7 flags that no lineage-corrected analysis was done. PATRIC's 1,595-strain M. tuberculosis pool is known to be Beijing-skewed because Beijing MDR strains are sequenced disproportionately during outbreak surveillance. The paper's headline 'reference-strain-agnostic' claim is only meaningful if the ML transfers across lineages — untested in both the paper and our replication.
open_questions.next_steps: Assign lineage via TB-Profiler / KvarQ SNP barcode. Run leave-one-lineage-out CV per drug: train on 6 lineages, test on the held-out lineage; report ROC-AUC per (drug, held-out lineage) cell. Flag any drug where held-out-Beijing performance drops >20 AUC points vs cross-validated performance — that drug's ML model is lineage-memorising, not resistance-learning.

open_questions.q: For the '24 new' non-canonical AMR signatures (e.g. ubiA/ethambutol beyond embB, rpoC/rifampicin beyond rpoB), what fraction validates against independent phenotypic drug-susceptibility testing (DST) on strains not in the training set, and does phenotypic-DST validation distinguish true resistance-conferring mutations from compensatory/fitness-restoring mutations that co-segregate with resistance but do not themselves confer it?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §4.3 confirms ubiA (rank 24) and rpoC (rank 2) as SVM-only recoveries for ethambutol and rifampicin respectively. But rpoC is a known *compensatory* locus for rpoB fitness cost in rifampicin-resistant strains — it co-segregates with rpoB mutations without independently conferring resistance. The paper's SVM cannot distinguish causal from compensatory signal. Without phenotypic-DST validation on strains carrying the SVM-flagged non-canonical mutation *without* the canonical primary mutation, the '24 new signatures' remains a hypothesis-generating list, not a validated marker set.
open_questions.next_steps: For each of the 24 novel signatures, identify held-out strains in a public MIC dataset (CRyPTIC consortium 2022 has ~20,000 M. tuberculosis strains with quantitative MIC + WGS) that carry the SVM-flagged variant *without* the canonical primary-gene variant. Compare MIC distributions to matched wild-type controls. Any variant that does not shift MIC in the absence of the primary mutation is compensatory, not causal — reclassify it. CRyPTIC data is public/free; requires a separate replication pass.
